title: Marmaduke and the Moonbeam Crumbs
markdown:
The snowy mountains were very quiet and lovely. Soft moonbeams covered the tall peaks with pretty silver light that seemed to hum like a lullaby. Marmaduke, a young ogre who loved warm naps and even warmer cookies, felt a little happy feeling wiggling in his tummy. A beautiful quiet night, perfect for a little walk.

On his wide soft shoulder sat Corvus, a little bird with feathers like shiny black wool, always ready with a word or two.

“Be careful where you are stepping, Marmaduke,” whispered Corvus, puffing his chest. “That bluebell wood can be very twisty and turny in the dim light, and you wouldn’t want to stumble.”

Marmaduke smiled a slow gentle smile. Large soft hands, quiet grace on the mossy path. The bluebells, which usually waved hello in the day, now shimmered like many tiny sleeping bells in twilight shades. Then, looking down: a single tiny crumb, glowing with a soft warm light, right on the path. Interesting. Perhaps, just perhaps, a little bit yummy.

“Ooh, a glowing crumb!” A happy low rumble. “Where do you think it came from, Corvus? It’s so wonderfully bright.”

“Maybe it fell from a passing star.” Head tilt, looking carefully. “It’s not from the baker down the lane. We should follow it. The most sensible thing on such a splendid moonlit night.”

So Marmaduke, with Corvus bobbing like a little captain on his shoulder, followed the trail. Crumbs twinkled like tiny fallen stars, each one winking a soft hello, leading gently away from the usual path, deeper into the hushed rustling bluebell wood. Sweet air: damp earth after rain, sleepy perfume of flowers tucking in. Marmaduke did not feel worried, not even a little. Moonlight made everything look friendly. The crumbs were little winks, guiding him onward.

A soft rustle of leaves, a gentle whisper of breeze, a clearing. In the middle, a tiny cottage, mossy roof, a window spilling warm light that seemed to hum with coziness. Outside the door, stirring a large steaming pot with a sturdy wooden spoon: a little goblin in a tall floppy hat that nodded along with his movements, nose twitching whenever he smelled something wonderfully nice. A baker. The whole little house smelled of warm sugar, gentle spices, and all the happy feelings in the world.

“Well, hello there, my dear friends!” Warm as a crackling fire. “Have you lost your way, perhaps? Or are you following my special moonbeam crumbs? They do have a way of leading lovely travellers to my door.” A chuckle like smooth pebbles tumbling. “Captured moonlight and the sweetest of dreams, mixed with just a little bit of wonder.”

Marmaduke’s wide kind eyes widened further. “They are very pretty. And they lead us somewhere so lovely.”

“And quite yummy, too, I assure you!” A merry wink, eyes like the stars. He held out a warm glowing crumb, pulsing, radiating a soft warmth. “For a brave and gentle adventurer. Just one is enough to make your tummy feel perfectly warm and your heart wonderfully full of happy thoughts.”

Marmaduke took it carefully in his large soft palm. Warm, like a tiny piece of sunshine. When he nibbled, it tasted of the sweetest honey, moonlight, and being perfectly safe. Corvus pecked a tiny polite piece and nodded with a definite air of approval.

“Thank you ever so much.” Drowsy warmth, a blanket tucked around his shoulders.

“My pleasure, my dear ogre. Now, I do believe it’s best you be getting home. The moon is climbing, and your own cozy bed will be waiting patiently.”

A grateful wave. Homeward. The path seemed even brighter. Bluebells whispered soft lullabies. Corvus was much quieter now, perhaps feeling the dreamy magic too. Marmaduke walked with a steady peaceful pace, tummy perfectly content. The wood felt like a whispering friend. The mountains felt like a hug.

Soon, home, fire embers like sleepy scattered stars. Mossy bed. Corvus on his favourite perch, feathers shimmering. Moonlight painted gentle dancing patterns on the floor. Marmaduke closed his eyes on glowing crumbs and a floppy hat, and did not need the night to tell him it had been enough. A last crumb, if there was one in a pocket, would keep until morning, which is a kind of moonlight too.
